page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highmem-8 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs and 64 GB of system memory. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, the instance features 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPU accelerators, and it is provisioned with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

In benchmark evaluations, the n2d-highmem-8 demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% of tested systems via stress-ng. Multi-core CPU performance and memory bandwidth benchmarks, including read-only small block cached speeds of 509.47 GB/sec and uncached large block write speeds of 40.87 GB/sec, fall within the average tier. Similarly, Geekbench scores, Passmark database operations, and static web serving throughput align with middle-tier expectations. However, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and prompt processing for medium-sized 7B language models represent performance bottlenecks, registering in the bottom 25% of benchmarks.

With a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core, this instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high compute density. By avoiding the overhead of additional vCPUs, users can run memory-bound applications economically. The hardware profile and benchmark results make the n2d-highmem-8 suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching, enterprise application hosting, and moderate data processing tasks.

With 4 physical cores and 2 threads per core, it allocates dedicated CPU resources supported by a 32 MB L3 cache. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, while multi-core execution, memory bandwidth, and database operations perform in the average tier. Conversely, multi-threaded decompression and medium-model LLM prompt processing show weaker relative performance. This resource profile provides qualitative cost efficiency for memory-heavy workloads by offering 8 GB of RAM per vCPU. It is best suited for databases, caching layers, and general-purpose memory-bound enterprise applications.
